blocks.instruction: Read each situation carefully and answer the questions.

items.label: (a)
items.q: As they entered the village, the children saw trees full of bright orange-red flowers. Name the tree and explain why it has its special name.
items.answer: Palash (1). When its flowers bloom, the whole forest looks reddish-orange from far away, so it is called the 'flame of forest' (1).

answerPoints.point: Forest looks reddish-orange like a flame

items.label: (b)
items.q: Amit said, 'These houses look so different from houses in the city.' What were the village houses made of, and what was the wall painting made with?
items.answer: Clay, hay, cow dung and other natural materials (1). The painting was done with a dye of rice flour mixed with water (1).

items.label: (c)
items.q: In the house, grains were stored in earthen pots and bamboo baskets. What was special about the way these containers were prepared, and why?
items.answer: Earthen pots were lined inside with neem leaves and bamboo baskets were coated with cow dung on the outside (1). This keeps the stored grains protected from insects and pests (1).

answerPoints.point: Neem leaves inside pots; cow dung on baskets
Protects grains from insects and pests

items.label: (d)
items.q: Dada ji took out a bottle of liquid and rubbed it on the children's hands and feet before the celebration. What was it and why was it used? Name one thing from the market that does the same job.
items.answer: A mixture made with neem oil, used so that mosquitoes do not bite (1). Mosquito repellent cream from the market (1).

answerPoints.point: Neem oil mixture to stop mosquito bites

items.label: (e)
items.q: Imagine there is no electricity in your area for two days. Write two changes you would see in your daily life.
items.answer: Any two sensible changes (1 each): no fans or lights at night; no TV or phone charging; water pumps may not work; food in the fridge may spoil; more time outdoors or with family.

blocks.instruction: Answer the following questions in two or three sentences.

items.label: (i)
items.q: What is Gond art? How are the paints for it made?
items.answer: Gond art is a form of painting on walls using natural colours (1). The artists make pictures of nature like trees, animals, birds and humans (1). The paints are made from natural extracts of flowers and leaves and powdered coloured stones (1).

answerPoints.point: Pictures of trees, animals, birds, humans
Paints from flowers, leaves, powdered coloured stones

items.label: (ii)
items.q: Who are the Jenu Kurubas? What do they do that shows their respect for nature?
items.answer: The Jenu Kurubas are a tribe from Karnataka (1). Their name comes from 'Jenu', which means honey, and they collect honey from beehives (1). While collecting honey they sing songs to apologise to the bees, showing respect for nature (1).

items.label: (iii)
items.q: What things should be kept in a first-aid box? Why is first aid important?
items.answer: Bandages, cotton, antiseptic liquid or cream, some medicines, mosquito repellent cream, a pair of scissors (2 for at least four items). First aid gives quick help to an injured person before the doctor comes and stops the injury from getting worse (1).

items.label: (iv)
items.q: What are Sacred Groves? Why are they important?
items.answer: Sacred Groves are small patches of forest protected by local communities (1). The trees and wildlife inside them are preserved (1). They are important places for the community to gather, worship and celebrate the beauty of nature (1).

answerPoints.point: Small forest patches protected by community

items.label: (v)
items.q: What challenges arise when we overuse natural resources? Give three examples.
items.answer: 1 mark each: overusing wood makes forests deplete; overusing water dries up rivers and wells; overusing soil (too much farming/digging) makes it poor; overfishing reduces sea life.

blocks.instruction: Complete the table in your answer book.

items.q: Copy and complete the table: for each plant write the part used and one use — Tulsi, Ajwain (carom), Neem, Marigold, Amla.
items.answer: Tulsi – leaves – cures cough and cold / tea; Ajwain – seeds – helps digestion, stomach ache; Neem – leaves/oil – keeps insects and mosquitoes away, skin care; Marigold – flowers – natural dye, decoration; Amla – fruit – rich in vitamin C, good for health. 1 mark per row (½ part, ½ use).

items.label: (ii)

items.label: (i)
items.q: Houses made of natural materials like clay and hay are good for a village.
items.answer: Natural materials are easily available nearby and cost less (1). They keep the house cool in summer and do not harm the environment (1).

items.label: (ii)
items.q: We should say no to plastic.
items.answer: Plastic does not rot and stays in the soil and water for years, polluting them (1). Animals may eat plastic and get hurt or die (1).

items.label: (iii)
items.q: People in different parts of our country worship plants and animals.
items.answer: It shows our rich tradition of respecting and protecting nature (1). Worshipping trees like the banyan or animals like the elephant helps people care for them and not harm them (1).

items.label: (i)
items.q: How was the natural paint on grandmother's cloth made?
items.answer: From natural extracts of flowers and leaves (1) mixed with powdered coloured stones (1).

items.label: (ii)
items.q: What did the people do before the festivities started in the evening? What were they wearing?
items.answer: They gathered in a big field and offered prayers to God and mother nature (1). They wore traditional clothes and jewels (1).

answerPoints.point: Prayers to God and mother nature

blocks.instruction: Answer in detail (five to six sentences).

items.label: (i)
items.q: Write the steps to prepare a natural dye and use it to colour a piece of cloth.
items.answer: Collect flowers, leaves, barks or roots that have colour, such as beetroot, hibiscus or marigold (1). Boil them in 1–2 litres of water for 30 minutes to an hour with the container covered, with the help of an elder (1). Strain the liquid to remove the plant material — this is the dye (1). Soak a light-coloured cloth in the dye overnight (1). Squeeze and dry it the next morning (1).

answerPoints.point: Boil 30–60 min, covered, with elder's help

items.label: (ii)
items.q:
How can we protect the natural environment around us? Write five ways.
OR
Describe the celebration in Reena and Amit's village in the evening. What did the children learn about the villagers' connection with nature?
items.answer: First option — 1 mark each for five ways: plant trees; keep food and water for birds; say no to plastic; reduce paper waste; organise clean-up drives; spread awareness; save water. OR option: the village was lit with colourful lights (1); everyone gathered in a big field in traditional clothes and jewels (1); prayers were offered to God and mother nature (1); dhol and nagada played and everyone danced (1); the children saw the beautiful connection the villagers had with nature and thought about how to thank nature (1).
items.markingGuide: Five correct, sensible sentences — 5; three or four — 3; one or two — 1.

items.q: Design your herbal garden. Draw at least three herbs or medicinal plants (for example tulsi, ajwain, neem, aloe vera, mint) and write their names.
items.answer: Three plants drawn (1), all three named correctly (1), neat and coloured with a garden layout (1).
items.markingGuide: Three named plants, neat — 3; two plants named — 2; one plant or unlabelled — 1.

items.q: Reena and Amit wanted to thank nature for everything it gives. Write three things you would do to thank and care for nature in your own locality.
items.answer: Any three sensible actions (1 each): plant and water a sapling; keep water and grains for birds; refuse plastic bags; not waste paper; clean the park with friends; not pluck flowers or harm animals.
